To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nurse-reported adverse events can be summarized by two latent constructs: patient safety and nursing workload.

the nurse-reported adverse event data are multivariate multivariate and that a multilevel factor analytic model should be fitted to the data to assess the relationship between patient and safety and the nursing unit level and nurse level factors.

the relationship between patient outcomes and nurse staffing is mediated by patient safety, as indicated by nurse-reported adverse events, and that the relationship between nurse staffing and patient safety is moderated by nursing unit level factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of multivariate multilevelfactor analytic models for assessing patient safety.
the use of factor analytic models for multilevel structured data.
the application of multilevel confirmative factor analysis to the study of the relationship between nurse staffing and adverse events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multivariate multileveled nature of these data must be taken into account when analysing them.
the nurse-reported patient safety is not related to the nurse-reported adverse events.
a two-level confirmatory factor analysis model with two factors is the appropriate model to assess the relationship between patient outcomes and patient safety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multivariate multileveled nature of the nurse-reported adverse event data should be taken into account in the analysis.
the Bayesian multilevel factor analytic approach is a promising method for the analysis of multivariate multileveled data in the field of patient safety.

a multilevel factor analytic model with latent factors for adverse events and patient-safety-related behaviours at both the nurse and the nursing-unit level provides an appropriate framework to assess the relationship between adverse events and patient outcomes.

the multileve nature of the data must be taken into account when assessing the relationship between adverse events, patient safety and nurse staffing.
the use of multivariate multileval data requires multilevel factor analytic modelling to avoid biased inferences.
the Bayesian multilevel factor analytic approach is an appropriate tool for analysing multivariate multileveled data.
